correctness.rationale: The induced-path closure condition is exactly no excluded vertex adjacent to a nonadjacent selected pair. Complete-join case splitting proves the cograph polynomial recurrence, with all remaining cases forcing full opposite components. Universal-vertex decomposition and a complete nine-type four-vertex trivially perfect enumeration prove five-vertex uniqueness; the star polynomial proves both sharp coefficient thresholds. Separate exhaustive verifier checked every cograph through six labelled vertices (6039) and the minimal example census (462 small trivially perfect graphs). Finite tests support but do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: The induced-path convex closure system in the 2022 classification is a natural convex geometry on trivially perfect graphs. Its closed-set rank distribution is a stronger invariant than the total count. An exact quadratic-arithmetic recurrence for every cograph and the first nonunimodal convex geometry in this graph-induced family locate a structural enumerative boundary, motivated by convex-geometry coefficient-shape questions rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
